name: File data protection classes
plain: Files are encrypted at rest, and whether an app can read them while the phone is locked depends on a protection class.
meaning: iOS has four data protection classes; Android has credential encrypted and device encrypted storage. This decides if background work can run before the first unlock.

android.persistence: Device encrypted storage available at boot; credential encrypted storage only after first unlock
android.note: Boot receivers before unlock see only device protected storage

ios.persistence: Class A complete: locked unreadable; B complete unless open; C until first auth (default); D none
ios.note: Default class is until first user authentication (C); background tasks after a reboot need C or lower

limits.headline: Can keep files locked until you unlock the phone, depending on how they are protected
limits.user_action: Nothing. You unlock your phone as usual
can: Encrypt files at rest on Android and iPhone
Keep files unavailable until your first unlock after a restart on iPhone
Keep some files in device protected storage on Android for use before unlock
Run background tasks on iPhone after restart only with the lower protection class
cannot: Open locked files from a boot task before you unlock, on Android credential storage
Skip protection by default on iPhone; the default is until first user authentication
Share locked files with other apps
Run iPhone background tasks on the strictest protected files after a reboot
limits.differs: iPhone uses protection classes. Android uses device protected and credential protected storage.

story.what_it_is: Decides whether an app's files can be opened while the phone is locked.

marketing.name: Data Protection
marketing.pitch: Pitch: files are encrypted with keys tied to your passcode, and some can only be opened when the phone is unlocked.

story.for_you: Your files are scrambled so that someone who steals your locked phone cannot read them. You may notice that some apps cannot sync until you unlock your phone after a restart.
story.for_makers: Makers pick how strongly each file is protected. Strong protection keeps data safe but stops background work while locked, so they choose per file based on need.

use_cases.example: A chat app protects stored messages so they cannot be read from a locked phone.
A bank app keeps tokens locked until you unlock the phone.
A health app keeps heart data under strict protection while the phone is locked.
A podcast app downloads new episodes in the background and needs a weaker protection class for that.
A workout app must save a run even when the screen locks, so it uses a class that works while locked.
A home app lets a doorbell alert open before first unlock using only non sensitive data.
A forensic tool fails to read files from a locked phone because of these classes.

story.android_note: Uses credential encrypted and device encrypted storage with direct boot.
story.ios_note: Four classes tied to the passcode, from complete protection to none.

technical_bounds: Background tasks after reboot are limited by class

history.change: File based encryption and Direct Boot introduced
